lines: The Company is maintaining its underlying full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $212 million to $216 million, which excludes the $14.0 million one-time revenue item recognized in the third quarter and represents 13% year-over-year growth at the midpoint of the range.
Including the one-time revenue item, the Company’s full-year 2026 revenue guidance is $226 million to $230 million.

CAGR from 2019 to 2025 $212M to $216M FY2026 underlying revenue guidance, up 13% at the midpoint; $226M to $230M including one-time payment. $137.6M, no debt Cash and short-term investments as of 3Q FY26, with no debt 3

desk.headline: Revenue up 52.5% to $69.0m, helped by a $14m one-off fee; underlying 2026 revenue outlook kept at $212-216m

other.label: Adjusted EBITDA
other.change: $5.0m excl. one-off fee; vs -$0.9m a year ago

results: Revenue rose 52.5% to $69.0m, but $14.0m of that was a one-off fee from a customer ending an advertising contract; without it revenue was a record $55.0m, up 21.6%.
Growth came from affiliate fees paid by TV distributors (up 77% to $14.3m) and brand licensing abroad; broadcast advertising grew only 3.1%, and digital revenue fell 4.1%.
Net profit was $15.2m ($0.12 a share) against a $4.1m loss a year ago, helped by the one-off fee and lower legal costs.
Adjusted EBITDA was $19.0m, or $5.0m without the one-off fee, a second straight positive quarter.
Cash and short-term investments stood at $137.6m with no debt; nine-month operating cash flow turned positive at $7.7m.

guidance.summary: Newsmax kept its underlying 2026 revenue guidance of $212-216m (about 13% growth at the midpoint). Including the one-off fee, the range is $226-230m.

points: Management points to affiliate contracts renewing at higher rates as the main growth driver, noting its fees per subscriber still trail rival news channels.
International brand licensing is expected to reach about $16m in 2026 (up 344%) and about $25m on an annualised basis; Newsmax Ukraine launched on 1 November.
Midterm political advertising is not expected to add meaningfully to 2026 revenue; the company is positioning for the 2028 presidential cycle.
Spending on programming, streaming (Newsmax+ and the free Newsmax2 channel) and AI content licensing continues, while legacy print and newsletter overhead is being cut.
call.source: Investor presentation filed with the results (Exhibit 99.2) and management comments in the press release

watch: Underlying revenue growth once the one-off fee drops out in Q4.
Pricing on upcoming affiliate contract renewals.
Whether licensing revenue reaches the roughly $16m expected for 2026.
